hyades.d: The nearest open star cluster to the Solar System, sharing a common trajectory through space.

coma-star-cluster.d: A loose, prominent open cluster located high above the galactic plane in Coma Berenices.

ursa-major-moving-group.d: A co-moving stellar kinematic group containing the core stars of the Big Dipper.

pleiades.d: Luminous young open cluster just beyond the 100-pc boundary, prominent in night-sky lore.

praesepe.d: One of the nearest open clusters, sharing similar age and proper motion to the Hyades.

ic-2602.d: Bright young open cluster surrounding Theta Carinae in the southern sky.

ic-2391.d: Compact open cluster in Vela visible to the naked eye.

alpha-persei-cluster.d: Young OB stellar association surrounding Mirfak in Perseus.

m4-globular.d: The closest globular cluster to the Solar System, situated in Scorpius near Antares.

ngc-6397.d: One of the oldest known globular clusters in the Milky Way with a core-collapsed structure.

47-tucanae.d: The second brightest and most massive globular cluster in the Milky Way, located in Tucana.

omega-centauri.d: The largest and most massive globular cluster in the Milky Way; remnant nucleus of a dwarf galaxy.

m13-hercules.d: The premier northern sky globular cluster in the constellation Hercules; target of the 1974 Arecibo Message.

orion-nebula.d: The closest massive star-forming H II region to Earth, visible to the naked eye in Orion’s Sword.

ring-nebula.d: Iconic bipolar planetary nebula in Lyra ionized by a central white dwarf.

lagoon-nebula.d: Giant interstellar H II emission nebula and star-forming region in Sagittarius.

eagle-nebula.n: Eagle Nebula (M16 / Pillars of Creation / NGC 6611)
eagle-nebula.d: Active star-forming H II region in Serpens home to the iconic Pillars of Creation.

carina-nebula.d: One of the largest diffuse emission nebulae in our sky, containing Eta Carinae and the Cosmic Cliffs.

vela-snr.d: A massive expanding filamentary remnant of a stellar explosion occurring ~11,000 years ago.

cygnus-loop.d: Spectacular optical emission nebula marking a core-collapse supernova remnant in Cygnus.

crab-nebula.d: Pulsar wind plerion remnant created by the historical supernova of 1054 recorded by Chinese astronomers.

helix-nebula.d: The closest planetary nebula to Earth, showing a dying low-mass star shedding its outer gas shell.

dumbbell-nebula.d: The first planetary nebula discovered in history, notable for its bright hourglass morphology in Vulpecula.

local-interstellar-cloud.d: Partially ionised warm interstellar cloud (~7,000 K) in the Complex of Local Interstellar Clouds (CLIC) through which Sol is currently passing.

g-cloud.d: Neighboring warm interstellar cloud (~5,500 K) immediately adjacent to the LIC toward the Galactic Centre, enveloping the Alpha Centauri system.

blue-cloud.d: Compact warm diffuse cloud in the Complex of Local Interstellar Clouds situated along the line of sight to Sirius and Epsilon Canis Majoris.

aquilae-cloud.d: Warm local interstellar cloud in the CLIC extending toward the Aquila and Altair sector.

mic-cloud.d: Filamentary warm cloud (~9,900 K) heated by shock interaction at the interface between the Local Interstellar Cloud and the G-Cloud.

leo-cloud.d: Unusually cold (~20 K), dense neutral hydrogen ribbon embedded within the hot Local Bubble cavity at ~7.5 parsecs.

dor-cloud.d: Southern warm interstellar cloud in the Complex of Local Interstellar Clouds toward Dorado.

eri-cloud.d: Warm local interstellar gas cloud in the Eridanus sector of the CLIC.

vela-cloud.d: Fast-moving warm interstellar cloud in the southern Complex of Local Interstellar Clouds.

local-bubble.d: Low-density (~0.001 cm⁻³) interstellar cavity spanning ~200 pc across the Orion Spur, excavated by multiple Pleiades/Sco-Cen supernova explosions over the past 14 million years.

corona-australis-cloud.d: Compact, high-density molecular cloud complex hosting the young Coronet protostellar cluster at ~130 pc.

rho-ophiuchi-cloud.d: Dense dark nebula and active stellar nursery at the Upper Scorpius boundary of the Local Bubble, ~138 pc from Sol.

taurus-molecular-cloud.d: The nearest large molecular cloud complex and low-mass star-forming nursery on the rim of the Local Bubble.

pipe-nebula.d: Vast pipe-shaped dark molecular cloud complex in southern Ophiuchus silhouetted against the Galactic Bulge.

lupus-molecular-cloud.d: Chain of star-forming dark molecular clouds (Lupus I–IV) bordering the Scorpius-Centaurus OB association.

coalsack-nebula.d: The most prominent naked-eye dark absorption nebula in the southern Milky Way, silhouetted against Crux.

chamaeleon-cloud-complex.d: High-latitude southern molecular cloud complex rich in T Tauri protostars and reflection nebulae.

sagittarius-a-star.d: Supermassive black hole (4.15 million solar masses) at the dynamical center of the Milky Way galaxy.

geminga.d: Radio-quiet gamma-ray pulsar and neutron star created by an ancient local supernova.

psr-j0108-1431.d: One of the oldest and closest known isolated radio pulsars to Earth.

vela-pulsar.d: Rapidly rotating neutron star (period: 89 ms) powering the central filaments of the Vela SNR.

crab-pulsar.d: Young central neutron star (period: 33 ms) formed in the 1054 CE supernova at the heart of the Crab Nebula.
